sections.h2: Where can Nicholas County owners get answers on property tax?
sections.html:
Everything runs through the courthouse at 125 East Main Street, Carlisle. The PVA works from the basement, answers at 859-289-3735 and keeps hours from 8:30 to 4:30 on weekdays. The Sheriff's Office, at 859-289-3740, collects what is owed.

Mail to the PVA goes to P.O. Box 2, Carlisle, KY 40311. Its website carries the certified tax roll, a tax estimator, forms and a fee schedule, and the office says its goal is to help owners understand how assessments are built. The county's own sheriff page describes the job as public safety plus tax collection. Because the sheriff only collects, a dispute about a figure starts with the PVA.

sections.h2: How rural is Nicholas County for a homeowner?
sections.html:
Nicholas is among Kentucky's smallest and most rural counties. Carlisle is the seat and the only incorporated community, and the 2020 Census classed every resident as rural. Bourbon and Mason counties supplied the land in 1799, and 195 square miles of it are dry ground, with Bluegrass-style farms, wooded hollows and small villages.

History is close at hand. Forest Retreat, built in 1814, is a historic district on the National Register. A marker on U.S. 68 identifies the cabin Daniel Boone built in 1795 as his last Kentucky home. Blue Licks Battlefield State Resort Park, 148 acres shared with Robertson County near Mount Olivet, marks an August 1782 fight often called the last battle of the Revolution.

Jobs lie mostly elsewhere. Workers average 35.6 minutes to reach work, longer than in Montgomery, Muhlenberg or Nelson County. Only 82 employer establishments operate inside the county, with total employment of 415 in 2023, and retail sales for 2022 were $23,532 thousand, or $3,022 per resident. A buyer here is rarely tied to a local employer.

sections.h2: What does Census data show about Nicholas County housing?
sections.html:
The estimate for July 2025 is 7,949 people, up 5.5% from the 2020 base. In so small a county, a few sales can move the averages.

  • 3,355 housing units in 2025, and only 3 building permits that year.
  • Owners occupy 74.5% of homes in 2020 to 2024.
  • The Census midpoint for an owned house is $123,000.
  • Monthly owner costs are $1,143 with a mortgage and $426 without.
  • Gross rent has a midpoint of $728.
  • Household income has a midpoint of $59,531, with 16.2% of people in poverty.

Only 9.8% of adults past 25 have a four-year degree, and 10.3% of people under 65 have no health insurance. About 92.6% of residents stayed in place last year, the highest share of the four counties in the Census comparison used for this guide.

sections.h2: Who lives in Nicholas County households?
sections.html:
The county has 2,776 households averaging 2.74 people, larger than in the other three counties compared here. Children under 18 make up 24.9% of residents and people 65 and over 18.2%. Census Bureau data show 237 veterans, 17.1% of residents under 65 with a disability and 81.6% of households with a broadband subscription.

Self-employment matters. The Census Bureau lists 611 nonemployer establishments for 2024, many times the count of employer firms, so a seller may be dealing with a farm, a trade or a home-based business that shares the property. Horse farming also shapes the landscape: the 1954 Kentucky Derby winner Determine was bred on Forest Retreat Farm in the county. A seller with acreage should ask the PVA how land, barns and the house are classed on the roll before comparing values.

sections.h2: What does Nicholas County charge by date paid?
sections.html:
The PVA site announced that 2026 bills would be mailed on or about October 1, 2026. Payment steps follow KRS 134.015.

Nicholas County bill totals under the state due-date statute
Date paidConsequence
No later than November 1Two percent off the total
November 2 through year endThe total printed on the bill
During JanuaryFive percent added
Past January 31Ten percent added

The statute stops at 10%, though the Montgomery, Muhlenberg and Nelson County sheriffs each post 21% for the stretch between February and mid-April. Call 859-289-3740 for the figure that applies on your payment date.

Take an $800 bill. It costs $784 with the discount, $800 through December and $840 in January. At a 21% penalty it would be $968. The same statute describes the tax, fees, penalties and interest as a personal debt of the taxpayer from the assessment date until paid.

sections.h2: What steps lead to an assessment appeal in Nicholas County?
sections.html:
Ask the Nicholas County PVA or a deputy for a conference. KRS 133.120 requires it first, before or during the inspection window or any extension. The PVA must explain the constitutional and statutory rules and how the value was reached, and the office logs what was discussed.

KRS 133.045 keeps the tax roll open 13 days beginning the first Monday that falls in May. An owner who stays dissatisfied delivers a letter or petition to the County Clerk with the parcel, the reasons and an opinion of fair cash value, by the workday after the window closes. At the county hearing, an owner may record the audio. Filing never postpones payment. You pay on your stated value, and the final value decides what else is owed, with interest.

sections.h2: What homestead relief can Nicholas County seniors claim?
sections.html: Owners aged 65 and up, and owners classified as totally disabled by a federal agency or a retirement system, may claim the state deduction of $49,100 for tax years 2025 and 2026. Applied to the county midpoint of $123,000, it leaves $73,900 to be taxed. The PVA takes the application in the courthouse basement. Disability claims renew yearly, except for service-connected veterans and for owners found permanently and totally disabled by the federal Social Security Administration or the state retirement system.

sections.h2: Who receives the bill after a Nicholas County purchase?
sections.html:
According to the PVA, both value and ownership are pinned to the first day of January. A house bought afterward is billed to the previous owner until the next calendar year. The PVA tries to mail a copy to the buyer using information from a tax agreement signed by buyer or seller. A buyer who receives none can get a copy from the sheriff at 859-289-3740.

  • Seller: confirm the current bill is paid and keep the receipt.
  • Buyer: have a mailing address entered on the deed, as KRS 382.135 requires.
  • Both: put the year's tax split into the contract.
  • Estate sales: the executor lists heirs and estimated values in an affidavit at the County Clerk's office.

Unpaid tax can outlast a sale. KRS 134.015 says the lien from a delinquent bill runs up to eleven years under KRS 134.420, whoever holds title. A seller who suspects an old year is open should ask the sheriff before listing, and a buyer's title agent will want the answer anyway. With only three building permits issued in 2025, most buyers here are weighing older houses, so a clean tax record is one less thing to negotiate.

faqs.q: Where does Nicholas County keep its PVA?
faqs.a: The PVA works from the courthouse basement at 125 East Main Street in Carlisle, with weekday hours from 8:30 to 4:30 and a phone at 859-289-3735.

faqs.q: Who gets a Nicholas County bill after the house sells?
faqs.a: The previous owner is billed until the next calendar year, and the PVA tries to mail a copy to the buyer. A buyer with none can call the sheriff at 859-289-3740.

faqs.q: How much does paying early save in Nicholas County?
faqs.a: Two percent, if the whole bill is paid by November 1. After that the printed total is due through December 31.

faqs.q: What penalty follows January in Nicholas County?
faqs.a: KRS 134.015 sets 5% for January and 10% after January 31. Ask the sheriff for the exact payoff, since sheriffs elsewhere in Kentucky post 21% for the late winter and spring stretch.

faqs.q: What does the homestead exemption remove in Nicholas County?
faqs.a: The state takes $49,100 off assessed value once a qualifying owner applies at the PVA. Qualifying means 65 or over, or totally disabled, and the figure covers tax years 2025 and 2026.
